title: Nasruddin and the Sparrow
summary: A boy caught a sparrow and asked Nasruddin: "Mulla, is this bird alive or dead?" intending to crush it if Nasruddin said alive, or release it if he said dead....
full_text:
In the bustling Anatolian town of Akşehir, where donkey carts rattled through the spice bazaar and tea glasses clinked under the plane trees, lived Mulla Nasruddin. One afternoon, A boy caught a sparrow and asked Nasruddin: "Mulla, is this bird alive or dead?" intending to crush it if Nasruddin said alive, or release it if he said dead..... The local folk, who never missed an opportunity to hear the Mulla’s unexpected pronouncements, quickly formed an expectant circle around him, stroking their beards and whispering among themselves.

Seeing everyone staring at him with grave expressions, Nasruddin adjusted his voluminous turban with theatrical dignity. A crowd of curious onlookers gathered in a circle, eagerly anticipating how the Mulla would resolve the impossible dilemma. Rather than offering a conventional, boring answer that any dry scholar might recite, the Mulla approached the problem from an angle that no one in the village had ever dreamed possible.

With effortless timing and a completely straight face, Nasruddin delivered his masterstroke: With deadpan gravity and a twinkle in his eye, Nasruddin delivered his unforgettable verdict.  The entire square erupted into bewildered chuckles and hearty laughter, leaving the bewildered questioners shaking their heads in admiration, proving that true delight in nature leaves creatures free in their own skies.
moral: True delight in nature leaves creatures free in their own skies.
